articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Central Park Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Central Park tram stop towards Rochdale is currently out of service, affecting step-free access for passengers.
articles.content_html:
A lift at Central Park tram stop, which serves passengers travelling towards Rochdale via Oldham, is currently out of service. The disruption began on Tuesday, 28 July, at 6:06pm and will continue until further notice.

Customers travelling towards Oldham can access the Manchester-bound platform via lift from The Gateway and use the track crossing to reach the Oldham-bound platform. This arrangement is intended to assist those requiring step-free access.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the lift's unavailability. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes if necessary.

More information can be found on the Transport for Greater Manchester website.

articles.title: Rochdale's Local Plan to Shape Future with Thousands of New Homes
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's Local Plan aims to build nearly 11,000 new homes and transform transport hubs by 2039, with a council meeting scheduled to discuss its next phase.
articles.content_html:
A council meeting on July 28 will discuss the Rochdale Local Plan, which aims to shape the borough's future until 2039. The plan includes the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes around transport hubs.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy known as Places for Everyone, which aims to deliver around 175,000 homes across Greater Manchester over the next two decades. The plan is expected to attract investment and redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is central to the Local Plan, focusing on transforming land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This strategy includes plans for new public realms, community spaces, and improved walking and cycling routes.

The Local Plan also addresses various topics such as climate and energy, economic growth, and sustainable transport, prioritising the growth ambitions of Rochdale and its surrounding areas. The town centre is identified as a key area for regeneration, with recent developments including the £20m redevelopment of the Grade-I listed Rochdale Town Hall, which was completed in 2024. This redevelopment is expected to enhance the town's cultural offerings alongside other projects like the Touchstones Gallery.
